content.value_statement: Claude Code agents require exact frontmatter, tool scope, and activation guidance. This skill provides templates, validation rules, and review checklists for creating focused agents.
actual_capabilities: Explains the required Claude Code agent file location and Markdown structure.
Defines required and optional frontmatter fields for agent files.
Guides tool permission choices, including restricted Bash patterns.
Compares model choices for speed, reasoning depth, and inherited context.
Provides minimal and comprehensive agent templates for common workflows.
Includes validation checklists and troubleshooting steps for agent issues.
limitations: Does not run schema validation automatically.
Does not create a complete agent without user goals and project context.
Examples still require review before granting write, network, or shell access.
Schema guidance can become outdated if Claude Code changes its agent format.

use_cases.title: Create a Project Agent
use_cases.description: Build a focused Claude Code agent with clear activation rules, frontmatter, persona, and process steps.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Assistants
use_cases.description: Define repeatable agent patterns so a team uses consistent names, tool scopes, models, and review standards.

use_cases.title: Fix Agent Validation Issues
use_cases.description: Troubleshoot invalid names, missing descriptions, incorrect model values, and tool permission syntax.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Simple Agent
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a read-only Claude Code agent for reviewing TypeScript changes. Include name, description, minimal tools, model choice, persona, process, and validation checklist.

prompt_templates.title: Improve an Existing Agent
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Claude Code agent draft. Improve the description, persona, process, model choice, and tool permissions while keeping the agent focused on one task.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Secure Specialist
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Claude Code security review agent. Use least privilege tool access, clear severity reporting, concrete file references, and a process for avoiding unsafe fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Audit an Agent Set
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit these Claude Code agents for schema compliance, duplicate responsibilities, excessive tools, weak activation descriptions, and missing validation steps. Return prioritized recommendations.

output_examples.input: Create a simple code review agent for pull request checks.
output_examples.output: A focused agent specification with a lowercase name, concise activation description, read-only tools, balanced model choice, review process, and validation checklist.

output_examples.input: My agent is not activating when I ask for database review.
output_examples.output: A troubleshooting report that checks file location, frontmatter syntax, description specificity, model value, and the exact request wording used to invoke the agent.

output_examples.input: Review this team folder of agents for consistency.
output_examples.output: A governance summary covering naming conflicts, broad tool grants, missing personas, unclear responsibilities, and recommended consolidation opportunities.

best_practices: Give each agent one clear responsibility and a description that explains when to use it.
Grant the smallest tool set needed, especially for write, network, and shell access.
Include examples, process steps, and validation checks before publishing an agent.
anti_patterns: Creating broad helper agents that review, debug, refactor, test, and document everything.
Omitting tool restrictions when an agent only needs read-only analysis.
Using vague descriptions that do not tell Claude Code when to activate the agent.

faq.question: What does this skill help me create?
faq.answer: It helps create and improve Claude Code agents with valid structure, clear personas, correct frontmatter, and practical workflows.

faq.question: Does it support Codex users?
faq.answer: Yes. Codex users can apply the guidance when designing agent-style workflows, reviewing Claude Code agent files, or preparing marketplace content.

faq.question: Can it choose the right model for an agent?
faq.answer: It explains when to use sonnet, opus, haiku, or inherit based on task complexity, latency needs, and context requirements.

faq.question: Does it validate agent files automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides validation rules and checklists, but users must run or apply validation in their own tooling.

faq.question: How does it handle tool permissions?
faq.answer: It explains allowed-tools syntax and recommends granting only the permissions required for the agent task.

faq.question: When should I use a skill instead of an agent?
faq.answer: Use a skill for context-aware reference guidance. Use an agent for specialized workflows that need tools, process steps, and persistent context.
